title: a lineage
hook: a chain that runs back to the sun, and the Gita admits it broke
tomorrow: truth, discipline or study: what's worth teaching at home?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a lineage began with one honest sentence: Satyakama, who didn't know his line and said so. Today, a line that reaches back to the sun.
screen: `ONE HONEST SENTENCE.` · `TODAY: BACK TO THE SUN.`

segments.voice: Some family recipes come with a claim attached: this is how it was made back home, always. The Bhagavad Gita has a stranger claim than that. Krishna and Arjuna are in a chariot between two armies when Krishna says: what I'm telling you isn't new. I taught it long ago to Vivasvat, the sun. Two odd things in a row. How could he have taught the sun? And if the teaching is that old, why does Arjuna need it told again?
screen: `THIS IS HOW IT WAS ALWAYS MADE.` → `I TAUGHT THIS TO THE SUN.` → `TWO ODD THINGS.`

segments.voice: The chain comes at the start of the Gita's fourth chapter. Krishna taught this lasting yoga to Vivasvat. Vivasvat told it to Manu. Manu told it to Ikshvaku, a king. Handed down that way, the royal sages knew it. The Sanskrit for that handing down is parampara: one after another. Then the next line solves the second puzzle. Over a long stretch of time, Krishna says, this yoga was lost here. The Gita doesn't hide the gap. So he tells it again, today, to one person. Why him? Because, he says, you are my devotee and my friend. Arjuna catches the first puzzle himself. Your birth was later, he says, and Vivasvat's was earlier. How am I to understand that you taught him at the start? The Gita lets him ask it out loud. Krishna answers: many births have passed, for me and for you. I know them all; you don't. So a lineage, in this chapter, has three parts: a chain of people, a gap where the teaching goes quiet, and someone who picks it up again by speaking to the friend in front of him.
screen: `VIVASVAT, MANU, IKSHVAKU.` · `LOST OVER A LONG TIME.` · `TOLD AGAIN TO A FRIEND.` · `ARJUNA ASKS: HOW?`

segments.voice: Listen for the faintest sound you can find: a hum, a far car, your own breath. When it slips away, don't chase it; wait until it comes back on its own. Let it go quiet and return, the way the Gita lets a teaching go quiet and be spoken again.
A lineage: parampara, one after another. In the Gita, it can be lost, and told again.
For the road: a lineage. In the Gita, it begins again when one friend tells another.

fork.setup: you're Arjuna. Krishna has just said he taught this yoga to the sun, long ago. what do you say?

fork.reveal: Arjuna asks exactly that: your birth was later, Vivasvat's earlier. Krishna answers that many births have passed for both of them, and he remembers his.

original.note: Sanskrit: one after another. In Gita 4.2 the yoga comes down this way, from teacher to teacher.
